name: CA-35
label: Safe D

key_factors: Torres is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Democratic by six points
Cargile has raised under $5,000 with essentially no outside spending in the race
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98 percent
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a Democratic-leaning seat, an incumbent with a cash advantage of roughly 160 to 1, and markets pricing her win at about 98 percent. With no polling suggesting a contest, the forecast holds at a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any poll showing Cargile within single digits, or a late wave of outside spending against Torres, would be the first real sign of a race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Norma Torres enters the general election as the heavy favorite in a district that leans Democratic by six points on the partisan index. She has raised roughly $769,000 and holds about $339,000 in cash, while Republican Mike Cargile has raised under $5,000, with negligible outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put her chances near 98 percent.

Torres advanced to the general as the incumbent, and the fundamentals — party lean, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage — all point in the same direction. Cargile lacks the resources to introduce himself to voters or contest the seat seriously. The forecast expects a comfortable double-digit Democratic win, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
